It points to the model being utilized within the text-generation pipeline.
The tags indicate its relevance to the transformers and llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI for allegedly stealing hardware secrets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the AI startup of stealing proprietary hardware secrets.
The complaint alleges a pattern of trade secret theft by OpenAI employees who previously worked at Apple.
The lawsuit also names IO Products, the hardware venture founded by Jony Ive, as a defendant.

stories.title: Nvidia’s biggest RAM supplier just had a trillion-dollar debut on Wall Street
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SK Hynix, a major RAM supplier to the AI boom, successfully debuted on Wall Street.
The IPO was highly successful, raising $26.5 billion and surpassing Alibaba's record for a foreign company debut.
The news highlights the critical role of memory chip suppliers in the accelerating demand driven by AI.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI, accuses ex-employees of stealing trade secrets
stories.author: stock_toaster
bullet_points: Apple is taking legal action against OpenAI.
The lawsuit centers on accusations that former employees stole trade secrets.
This signals escalating intellectual property disputes within the competitive AI industry.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million in a funding round.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into personal AI development.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance.
This integration specifically targets and optimizes performance on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI capabilities for coding assistance.

stories.title: Meta turns off the Instagram feature that let users make AI deepfakes of public accounts
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta is disabling an Instagram feature that allowed users to create AI deepfakes using content from public accounts.
The feature faced significant backlash because it used public content without the account owner's explicit permission.
This marks a notable industry response to ethical concerns surrounding generative AI and data usage rights.

stories.title: The FCC is cracking down on DJI tech that dodged the foreign drone ban
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC is actively cracking down on entities suspected of circumventing the US foreign drone ban.
The crackdown targets companies like Xtra and Skyrover, which allegedly facilitate the entry of DJI technology into the US.
This signals increased regulatory scrutiny over foreign technology imports, specifically in the drone sector.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced through continuous processor recalibration.
Reinforcement learning is employed to leverage error information for algorithm adjustment.
This represents a significant step toward stabilizing and improving quantum computing hardware.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers he was hired to represent.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for betraying the victims.
The story highlights the severe risks and ethical breaches within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for safety-critical incident reasoning in autonomous driving.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of scene understanding and decision-making in autonomous systems.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Current LLM evaluation post-quantization relies too heavily on accuracy and perplexity, which are insufficient.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to assess behavioral changes caused by quantization.
This metric measures the overlap in correct predictions between a base model and its quantized versions, offering a more robust evaluation method.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: Introduces ARDY, a new autoregressive diffusion model designed for real-time 3D human motion generation.
Addresses the critical trade-off between offline methods (high control, slow inference) and online methods (fast inference, low control/semantics).
Aims to enable realistic, controllable, and fast motion synthesis crucial for robotics, simulation, and interactive applications.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training is effective, showing isolated training of these weights causes accuracy collapse.
Demonstrates that the concept of Super Weights and their importance is not universally applicable across all LLMs (e.g., OLMo-1B and OLMo-7B).

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations of current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks involving LLMs and multimodal models.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to enhance LLM-based web search.
It addresses limitations of single ReAct agents, which struggle with balancing search depth and coverage.
The system aims to overcome existing multi-agent weaknesses, particularly in achieving recursive search depth.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches its limit.
It proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
UltraX aims to overcome limitations in existing data refinement methods, such as the rigidity of rule-based approaches.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically boosting capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery demonstrated a new methodology for achieving reusability.
The effort is noted as an attempt to replicate successful technologies pioneered by SpaceX.

stories.title: Firmware update bricks Hue Bridge Pro devices; Philips gives free replacements
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A firmware update has caused Hue Bridge Pro devices to become unusable (bricked).
Philips is providing free replacement units to affected customers.
Users will face the inconvenience of reconfiguring all their connected lights and settings.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a method designed to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a novel way for models to unfold logical consequences across temporally connected video frames.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for CoF reasoning despite being trained on general corpora.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to reason about scientific lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking both scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation capabilities in AI systems.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and study mode, using data from 77,543 students.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows (tool use, branching, checkpointing).
The model is inspired by Lisp, utilizing symbolic forms and object identity as explanatory frameworks.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to better manage the state and context across complex LLM workflows.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on moral concepts, even compared to much larger open models.
The paper cautions that high agreement only proves reliability, not the validity of LLMs as accurate annotators for complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that good forward-marginal error in diffusion models guarantees numerical stability during sampling.
It demonstrates that a small $L^2$ error in the forward process does not ensure the learned reverse-time sampler is stable or well-behaved.
The research confirms that even with minimal forward error, the reverse-time process can be nonexplosive and closely approximate the true reverse process.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this hidden graph can enhance data sensemaking and analysis capabilities.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses only on geometric accuracy, neglecting biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The application has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' to organize information for better control reasoning.
Utilizes Autoregressive Variational Inference to enable adaptive decision-making in control tasks.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model specifically designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses limitations of existing methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: A new, publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM, AMALIA, is being tested as a data annotator for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The study highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and true validity when using LLMs for inferring theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in long trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for decision-making.
Focuses on surfacing scattered, decision-relevant state information (facts, goals, past attempts) for agents.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems.
It focuses specifically on citation quality verification in deep-research systems, where LLMs must ground claims with cited sources.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when performing structured rubric tasks for source attribution.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting in speculative decoding.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent draft token distributions.
Aims to accelerate Large Language Model (LLM) inference by improving the accuracy and structure of the draft tokens used in speculative decoding.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053 instances) to study communication variability in health AI.
Highlights a key limitation in current chatbot development: reliance on simulated, cooperative patients.
Introduces a novel patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotional state, and conversational strategy.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory.
Proposes MAESTRO, a new method to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Distinguishes itself from existing pruning methods by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike dense transformer methods.

stories.title: SpaceX wants to launch 100k more Starlink satellites for 100x the bandwidth
stories.author: CrankyBear
bullet_points: SpaceX plans a massive expansion of its Starlink constellation.
The goal is to deploy 100,000 additional satellites.
This expansion aims to deliver a 100x increase in bandwidth capacity.

stories.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
stories.author: github.com via Vaelatern
bullet_points: PostgreSQL has been successfully rewritten in the Rust programming language.
The Rust implementation has achieved 100% pass rate on the existing Postgres regression tests.
This signals a significant step in modernizing and potentially improving the performance/safety of a major database system.

stories.title: I Analyzed 4,788 AI Coding Sessions — Here's Where Your Tokens Actually Go
stories.author: psycgod
bullet_points: The article analyzes a large dataset (4,788 sessions) of AI coding interactions.
It focuses on tracking how tokens are consumed across various AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider).
The content offers practical insights into the operational costs and usage patterns of AI coding assistants.
